title: 第十八章 铁柱算账
novel_title: 坟头开铺，我靠守墓重整阴阳两界
content_zh:
方怀仁逃了。

    梁二叔还想抵赖。

    他扶着祠堂柱子站稳，脸色惨白，却硬撑着冷笑。

    “一个逃走的道士，一个半疯的亡魂，一个小鬼抱着烧坏的账本，就想定我的罪？”

    沈清萝没理他。

    她先把梁正德和春桃暂时安置进引魂铃，再让宋砚封住祠堂门。

    白槿没来，她只能自己照玄司习惯补一份临时证物单。

    “断买地券一张，井中焦账半本，药渣一罐，反向镇魂符残片三枚，白袖半片，阴木钉三根。”

    铁柱一边听，一边记。

    梁二叔咬牙：“你倒像个堂官。”

    沈清萝头也不抬。

    “穷人接活，流程不清楚容易被赖账。”

    梁氏很快让人取来了梁正德书房暗格里的副账。

    去取账时，梁二叔的眼神像刀一样扫过去。若是从前，梁氏大概已经退了。

    这一次她没有。

    她亲自带人进书房，亲自开暗格，亲自把那本用蜡封住的账抱出来。她走得不快，可每一步都比之前稳。那本账封在蜡里，封口还留着梁正德的私印。梁氏拆开时，手抖得厉害。

    沈清萝没有接。

    “你拿着。”

    梁氏抬头。

    沈清萝道：“账在你手里。命，也得自己拿稳。”

    梁氏眼眶发红，点了点头。

    铁柱蹲在供桌前，把井中焦账和梁正德副账摊开。他很少一次说这么多话。

    所以当他开口时，所有人都听得格外清楚。

    “三月初九，买符，七两。”

    他翻过焦账，又翻副账。

    “副账记清虚外门香火，七两。对得上。”

    梁二叔脸色一沉。

    铁柱继续。

    “四月十二，请人，二十两。副账记夜修祖坟，人工二十两。对得上。”

    “五日后，阴木钉，三根，十二两。副账写祖坟镇木，十二两。对得上。”

    他停了一下，翻到最后一页。

    “五月廿三，药一剂，半两。”

    祠堂里静得连灯油炸开的声音都听得见。

    铁柱抬头看梁二叔。

    “这一笔，记在大爷命上。”

    梁氏闭上眼，泪滚下来。

    梁家族老们的脸色也彻底变了。

    二叔怒吼：“一个记账的小鬼……”

    铁柱抱紧账本。
content_en:
Fang Huairen escaped.

    Second Uncle Liang still wanted to deny it.

    He held on to the pillars of the ancestral hall and stood firm, his face pale, but he still managed to sneer.

    "An escaped Taoist priest, a half-mad soul, and a kid holding a burned ledger, all want to convict me?"

    Shen Qingluo ignored him.

    She first temporarily placed Liang Zhengde and Chuntao in the soul-inducing bell, and then asked Song Yan to seal the door of the ancestral hall.

    Bai Jin didn't come, so she could only make up a temporary evidence list according to Xuan Si's habit.

    "One piece of land purchase certificate, half a book of burnt accounts in the well, a jar of medicine dregs, three fragments of the reverse soul talisman, half a piece of white sleeves, and three yin wood nails."

    Tie Zhu listened and took notes.

    Second Uncle Liang gritted his teeth: "You look like a court official."

    Shen Qingluo didn't even raise her head.

    "Poor people take jobs, and the process is unclear and they are easily defaulted."

    Mrs. Liang quickly had someone fetch the deputy ledger from the secret room of Liang Zhengde's study.

    When he went to collect the bill, Uncle Liang's eyes swept over him like a knife. If it had been in the past, Liang would have probably retired.

    This time she didn't.

    She personally led people into the study, opened the secret compartment personally, and took out the account sealed with wax. She didn't walk fast, but every step was more steady than the previous one. The account was sealed in wax, with Liang Zhengde's private seal still on the seal. When Liang took it apart, her hands were shaking badly.

    Shen Qingluo didn't answer.

    "You take it."

    Liang raised his head.

    Shen Qingluo said: "The account is in your hands. You have to take care of your own life."

    Liang's eyes turned red and she nodded.

    Tie Zhu squatted in front of the altar table and spread out the Jiao account in the well and Liang Zhengde's deputy account. He rarely spoke so much at once.

    So when he spoke, everyone heard him very clearly.

    "On the ninth day of March, buy amulets, seven taels."

    He looked through the burnt accounts and then through the secondary accounts.

    "Deputy accountant Qingxu outer door incense, seven taels. That's right."

    Uncle Liang's face darkened.

    Iron Pillar continues.

    "On April 12, I asked for twenty taels. The deputy accountant repaired the ancestral tomb at night, and the labor cost was twenty taels. That's right."

    "Five days later, there will be three Yin wooden nails, twelve taels. The deputy account states that the ancestral tomb support wood, twelve taels. That's right."

    He paused and turned to the last page.

    "On May 23rd, one dose of medicine, half a tael."

    It was so quiet in the ancestral hall that you could even hear the sound of the lanterns turning on.

    Tie Zhu looked up at Uncle Liang.

    "This sum will be recorded in my life."

    Mrs. Liang closed her eyes and tears rolled down her face.

    The expressions of the elders of the Liang family also completely changed.

    The second uncle roared: "A little kid who keeps accounts..."

    Tie Zhu hugged the ledger tightly.
